Next mail release — where it lives
A · Pinned in the menu DefaultA fixture in the sidebar's foot — always there, never in the way. B · A strip on the pageThe banner over each mail-room page, as it was.
Rules — the shape of the section
A · Two sections DefaultGroup rules and Client rules; each opens on all of its types, and the rail narrows. B · Three, with an indexAn Overview page in front of the two.
Search — where the form lives
A · Inside Documents, in a drawer DefaultSearch leaves the menu; the whole form opens as a drawer from Advanced search. B · Its own page, form open TodayWhat the prototype had until now: Search as its own stop, the four groups top to bottom, nothing between the caller and the field. C · Inside Documents, unfoldingThe same door, with the form opening over the results instead of beside them.
Quick search — the five typed fields
A · One box for anything DefaultThe box names what it takes — claim, check, voucher, TIN, key or recipient — and you paste whichever one you have. B · A rail of named fieldsThe CAS quick search standing on the right, field by field, with the box still above the list.
ID card home — the table
A · The CAS zones DefaultTwo-storey header: transformation → composition & print → overall, chained. B · One row of columnsOur house style — the stages implied by the order, no second storey.
Naming — what the menu calls things
A · The new names DefaultFiles, Documents, Errors, Report library — named for what they do. B · The CAS namesFile Tracker, Document Manager, Error Manager — the muscle memory of everyone coming from CAS.
Test runs — where they live
1 · Always in the menu DefaultTest runs is its own entry, next to Rules. 2 · Behind the Test mode switchFlick it on below and the menu section appears; off, it folds away. 3 · A lane inside FilesBack inside Communications › Files: live and test as two lanes.

Products — how the shelf is ordered
A · Why you have each one DefaultThe provider portal's grammar: your contract as the root, then what came included, what you chose, and what you could add — status lives on the card, not in the shelf title. B · By product family TodayThe provider’s card grammar: the network on top, then Payments and Communications with their cards. C · Hierarchy stackingThe products nested under the network.

Wizard cards — how a configured type reports itself
A · Count beside Configure Default B · Full breakdown

A keeps every card two lines: the button rides in the header with the total beside it. B spends a second line on what is actually affected — levels, accounts and templates on a document; groups, rules, claims, recipients and documents on a rule type.

Onboarding wizard
Full flow (faithful) Default Compact summary
What we added
Plain names

Off → the platform’s own task name and its system description.

The fix, on the error

Off → the record, and nothing about solving it.

What the scheduled email carries
A · The report attached Default B · A link, file stays in the portal

A is what was asked for. B exists because the report names claims, recipients and states — the same question that took repair off the errors page.

Configuration & Client — how they merge
A · One Configuration, wizard above Default B · One Manage section, wizard inside as step 1

Both merge the two sections into three blocks — this client · how files arrive · what documents are made of. They differ on the wizard: beside the section, or the first thing in it.

Rule wording
Staged, not test

Off → the CAS words: test copy, Test only, Overwrite test with live. On, the copy that does not print is staged, and test is left to mean the run.

Repair
A · Not allowed Default B · Allowed

CAS purges and marks resolved; it does not repair, because repairing means opening a document and being able to change a check amount. A points those errors at their cause instead.

Actions
A · Inside the drawer Default B · Visible on the page

B also puts it on the board card. Faster — and easier to purge 37 documents without reading why.
